newsitem.title: USA: Judges seek conditions on PacTel merger.
newsitem.headline: Judges seek conditions on PacTel merger.

text.p: California's approval for the proposed merger between Pacific Telesis Group and SBC Communications Inc should be made conditional on a Pacific Telesis unit refunding $590 million to customers, judges who advise California regulators have recommended.
Two administrative law judges, who make recommendations to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), issued a proposed decision on the merger on Friday.
They recommended approval of the proposed $17 billion merger between Pacific Telesis and SBC on condition that Pacific Telesis unit Pacific Bell refund $590.5 million to ratepayers over five years.
The judges said this was half of the total economic benefits of the merger which they forecast at $1.18 billion.
The judges concluded that the merger was unlikely to affect competition adversely.
The CPUC is expected to vote on the merger next month. It can accept, modify or reject the judges' recommendation.
SBC and Pacific Telesis announced their merger plans last April. The CPUC's decision is the only regulatory approval still required.

A Pacific Bell spokesman could not be reached for comment on Saturday. But the San Francisco Chronicle quoted Pacific Telesis Chairman Phil Quigley as saying the proposed conditions were a "crippling penalty" which could "seriously jeopardize the merger" if adopted by the CPUC.

Consumer groups had called for refunds to customers of nearly $1 billion over five years, but the merging companies opposed this, saying the benefits of the merger would flow to ratepayers in the form of lower prices for telecommunications services.

The administrative law judges also proposed that Pacific Bell be required to make certain changes to an agreement it signed with community groups. Alternatively, they said, Pacific Bell could contribute $82 million to a trust designed to improve the telecommunications access and education of underserved communities in California.

The judges also recommended that Pacific Bell and SBC be required to undergo an audit of their accounting and record-keeping practices, create a trust for Pacific Bell employees' pension funds and reduce Pacific Bell's rates by $13 million.
